title: A runner never stops to wait for its own test run
goal: A runner sometimes finishes the work, starts the test run in the background, says it will carry on when the tests finish, and ends its turn. In this loop ending the turn ends the task: the work is put aside, the task counts as failed and goes back to the queue, and the next runner has to pick the pieces up. On 2026-09-23 this happened to the task the whole video rebuild waits on, with its audit already written. Make it stop happening, and make it cost nothing when it does.

acceptance: The time a full Scripts/test.sh run takes today is measured and written in this task's log, so the rule below is set against a real number

The runner rules say plainly that ending a turn ends the task, and say how to run the test run so it finishes inside the turn (in the foreground with a long enough timeout, or the named way that fits the measured time)

When a runner exits 0 with its task still in progress and its last words say it is waiting for something to finish, the loop gives that same session one more turn to finish instead of recording a failure, at most once per task, and the log says it did
A drill or test feeds the loop's exit handling a waiting last line like the four recorded ones and sees the resume rather than a failure
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: digest 2026-09-24: happened three times in the last 24 hours (history runner_failed, exit 0): the-video-mocks-are-the-user-s-again-and-d18-is 'I'll pick up again when it finishes', tracks-you-can-add-rename-group-hide-mute-lock-a 'Twelve right-click walks are running in the background', recordings-and-sounds-in-a-document-sit-on-the-l 'Full tests are still running'. Each cost a whole runner cycle on the focus. Moved to p1 so it is fixed before the next twenty focus tasks run.

measured: a full Scripts/test.sh at fa1f1ea4 took 220s wall (209s of tests, 9686 in 776 suites) at 19:45 on 2026-09-24, and 214s on a second run at 20:00. The rule is set against that: foreground with the Bash tool's timeout 600000 (the ten minute ceiling), about 2.7x headroom.

reproduced from the record rather than by running: queue/history.jsonl holds eleven runner_failed events with exit 0 whose last line says the runner was waiting (2026-09-02 to 09-24), not four. All eleven are in failure-drill.sh scenario 8 word for word. Checked for real that the CLI resumes a print-mode session: claude -p --session-id <uuid> then claude -p --resume <uuid>, and the second turn referred back to the first.

built: queue-lib runnerIsWaiting + decideRunnerResume (exit 0, task in_progress, no CLI refusal, last words waiting, once per claim keyed on task.started; logs the task, writes task.waitResume, emits runner_resumed). queue.mjs runner-resume prints RESUME=0|1. go-loop.sh starts every task runner under --session-id <uuidgen>, and resume_if_waiting runs queue/bin/resume-prompt.md in the same session with --resume before record_exit; the leftovers snapshot is not retaken on the resumed turn. runner-prompt.md has a new rule, 'Ending your turn ends your task', with the measured number.

verified: failure-drill.sh scenario 8 (new, 10 checks: resumed-and-finished, same session id, prompt wording, log + history, only once, quiet stop not resumed, all eleven recorded lines match, finished summaries do not) and scenarios 1-7 all pass; leftovers-drill, manager-due-drill, awake-drill pass; Scripts/test.sh green. The live loop adopts the go-loop.sh change between tasks by its own reload.

left rough, not filed: the digest and manager passes are not resumed (they have no task to be in progress; none of the eleven recorded cases was one). When a runner ends its turn with a job in the background, the CLI waits up to 600s for it and then kills it, so a resumed runner may have to run its tests again; the resume prompt tells it to. Neither is something a person would notice beyond what this task fixes.

first full test run hit the known flaky 'written twice, an animated export lands at the same size' (160386 vs 233688 bytes); folded into the-export-size-test-fails-about-one-run-in-thre. Second run green.
owns no walks; the ones it names are examples

Runner rule 'Ending your turn ends your task' in queue/bin/runner-prompt.md with the measured full test run (220s/214s, foreground, timeout 600000). go-loop.sh starts task runners under --session-id and, when one exits 0 with its task in progress and last words saying it is waiting, resumes the same session once per claim (queue/bin/resume-prompt.md) before recording the exit; task log + runner_resumed event say so. Verified by failure-drill.sh scenario 8 (real loop, fake runner: waits once -> resumed and done; waits twice -> one resume then failure; quiet stop -> no resume; all eleven recorded waiting lines match), scenarios 1-7, leftovers/manager-due/awake drills, and a green Scripts/test.sh.
